changelog_review.accuracy: Names exactly the Linux signal mask/stdin/stdout fatal setup paths changed in production.
changelog_review.benefit: Explicitly states prevention of failed children executing controller code; supported by terminal _exit source and fault assertions.
changelog_review.entry: - **[Worker lifecycle]** Made Linux replay children terminate on signal mask or stdin/stdout setup failure so failed workers cannot execute controller code. ([#56](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/56))
changelog_review.preservation: All inherited entries and open-PR-is-not-merged-delivery qualification preserved byte-for-byte after removing only the new entry and its separator.
changelog_review.scope: No scheduler, Windows, Steam, performance, GPU or broad recovery claim.
changelog_review.topic: Worker lifecycle is the concise meaningful parent46 topic.

AC1.rationale: Every covered fatal setup path is terminal and child-safe; production faults and controls independently prove process ownership, exact statuses, cleanup/reaping and no unintended worker spawning. Neighboring branches and full integrated compatibility/matrix/changelog gates pass.

limits.reason: Explicit inherited user exclusion, no native Windows claim.

publication_gate: Deferred to coordinator after this final acceptance; remote PR65 intentionally old head until authorized normal publication. Only56 eligible close; parent46 stays open. No merge approval inferred.

assertions: No injection or controlled crash; two initial controller-owned nonempty workers each exit zero through the actual worker path and are controller-reaped exactly once.
Readback-checked fixture contains shader 0x101, layout 0x102 and compute hashes 0x104/0x105; both pipelines are parsed and completed using the real null device.

Controller exits zero, progress_complete one, clean/dirty deaths zero, exact protocol EOF and setup sequence, expected inherited stream flush only by normal workers, no fallthrough/unexpected births/survivors.
fork-child-healthy.evidence: Independent four full133 suites executed this ID with active assertions, failures0/skips0; DebugOFF also three actual repeat starts. See matrix gate records and inventory.

assertions: No setup fault. Generation one performs setup/protocol EOF then reports zero cursors and zero culprit hashes and exits two. Production process_shutdown and actual recovery launch generation two over the full original two-pipeline assignment.

Replacement executes real run_slave_process and successfully parses/completes both fixture pipelines; assert counters equal two, not number of normal workers one. Controller exits zero, progress_complete one, clean deaths one, dirty deaths zero.

Exactly two controller-owned births, original-controller reaps with statuses two then zero, no fatal sentinel callbacks/flush, exact protocol EOF and no descendants. This verifies a no-progress retry followed by real complete recovery, not a fictional completed prefix or skipped culprit.
fork-child-healthy-recovery.evidence: Independent four full133 suites executed this ID with active assertions, failures0/skips0; DebugOFF also three actual repeat starts. See matrix gate records and inventory.

assertions: Exactly one injection at the intended production child syscall, PID and generation; failed child exits normally with EXIT_FAILURE, never returns through the Boolean launcher.
Every birth belongs to the original controller; exactly two births and one controller reap per worker, no worker-owned fork or worker epoll/controller operation, no observer-adopted descendants.
No inherited atexit/destructor invocation or buffered-stdio flush by fatal setup; no normal run_slave_process entry for the failed child.

Exact setup order and required protocol EOF; failed worker and controller are collected, every recorded PID is gone, observer obtains ECHILD, bounded event EOF and emergency group cleanup remain active on assertion failure.
Controller returns EXIT_FAILURE and shared progress_complete remains zero for lost required work, consistent with new master #13; no old aggregate-success oracle.

The other initial worker completes its nonempty partition through real null-device replay and is successfully controller-reaped before releasing the selected fault; assert that event ordering, two initial births, exactly one completed/parsed pipeline, dirty deaths one and clean deaths zero.
